correctness.rationale: Exact stationarity eliminates each private nutrient and consumer density in favor of the global nutrient R, while the total resource–biomass balance yields R0=H(R). Its derivative is strictly positive on each support interval; continuity and divergence at the accessible resource ceiling imply a unique selected equilibrium. Any skipped species with qi<R has a positive rare-invasion eigenvalue. For the constructed initial-segment support, the weighted quadratic linearized energy has strictly dissipative nutrient blocks with determinant ((1-Ti/R)(3+Ti/R))/(4Ti^2), and its only invariant zero-dissipation state is zero. All excluded invader eigenvalues are negative off the sharp supplies. The proof establishes arbitrary finite S analytically; exact rational checker passes displayed example and 800 supplementary stationary cases. The theorem excludes the zero-eigenvalue entry boundaries and does not claim global attraction.

value.rationale: Exact source-dependent supply values decide which ecological competitors can persist at an attracting equilibrium, and the finite resource ceiling proves that no amount of enrichment can rescue sufficiently demanding species when niche separation remains incomplete. This answers the source paper’s motivated intermediate-isolation/multi-species analytical gap and distinguishes hard diversity limits from resource insufficiency. Arbitrary finite species counts, unique selected local sink and strict comparative statics give a structural classification rather than a routine small example or numerical replot.
